key_insight: Adaptive Power Sampling tunes the sharpening exponent per query, using answer agreement and self-reward gap to decide when extra sharpening helps reasoning.
engineering_relevance: This gives a training-free way to improve LLM reasoning at inference time while avoiding a one-size-fits-all decoding setting.
method: Measure the model's answer agreement as a proxy for confidence/consensus.
Use the relation between agreement and self-reward gap to choose a query-specific sharpening exponent.
Sample from the sharpened distribution adaptively instead of using a fixed exponent for all queries.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on MATH500, HumanEval, and GPQA, where it consistently beat fixed-exponent power sampling in the abstract's reported results.
watch_item: Because APS depends on estimating agreement/self-reward at test time, its benefit may be sensitive to calibration and added inference-time computation.
paper_title: Adaptive Power Sampling for LLM Reasoning
